response: Yes, there is an association between recurrent spontaneous abortion and skewed X-inactivation. Skewed X-inactivation, which refers to the preferential inactivation of one X chromosome over the other, has been observed in some women with recurrent spontaneous abortion. This phenomenon is thought to be related to the abnormal expression of X-linked genes, which can affect embryonic development and increase the risk of miscarriage. Studies have suggested that women with recurrent spontaneous abortion are more likely to have skewed X-inactivation, particularly in their peripheral blood cells. However, the exact mechanisms underlying this association are still not fully understood and require further research.
